rationale: The dominant ground-truth thread is the scoping risk of making vllm_c the global CUDA default when only validated on Qwen-Image/H200 (hsliuustc0106's main comment, plus NumberWan's FLUX.1-dev justification) — Y directly engages this, correctly traces the per-model override safety net (cosmos3) and cites the same FLUX.1-dev evidence reviewers demanded, while X never mentions scoping at all. X's two findings (stale pytest.mark.core_model, backend-agnostic test gap) are valid and concretely actionable, matching Gaohan123's 'pytest mark is not complete' comment, but that's a narrower slice of the ground truth. Both reviews are well-grounded in the diff with no fabrication; X is slightly more surgically actionable per-line, but Y's higher recall on the PR's central concern outweighs that.
